problem: End-to-end 3D referential grounding models need large annotated text-to-3D data and overfit to dataset syntax; LLM-based zero-shot methods handle spatial/mathematical reasoning poorly (e.g. picking smallest x for 'left'), rely on benchmark-specific prompt engineering, and assume clean meshes rather than noisy real-time maps.
motivation: Robots need to ground free-form references with spatial relations and attributes in unseen scenes, but 3D language data is scarce. Observations: VLMs supply fine-grained 2D attributes (color, material) that 3D perception misses, and LLMs are good at sequential reasoning but bad at geometry, so geometry should be delegated to rule-based functions.
key_idea: Have an LLM decompose a referring expression via chain-of-thought into calls to a heuristic spatial-reasoning toolbox over a filtered object list enriched with 2D VLM captions, achieving zero-shot 3D grounding with a single in-context example.
insight: Delegating spatial logic to deterministic tools and adding 2D captions is what makes zero-shot grounding work. The caption ablation on Nr3D (GPT-4o) raises the method from 54.5 to 60.5 overall and view-dependent from 50.7 to 56.6, and also helps Transcrib3D (58.5 to 61.0), showing that attributes missing from 3D perception are a bottleneck. Gains are largest on IRef-VLA Hard (75.0 vs 57.5 for Transcrib3D), which is attribute-heavy; the method trails Transcrib3D on overall accuracy, which uses benchmark-tailored principles.
method: Instance-level semantic mapping: Grounding DINO + SAM2 2D detection/segmentation, LiDAR points projected to pixels, 2D tracking plus 3D proximity to build instance point clouds/3D boxes (GT boxes used on ReferIt3D).
2D captioning: for each object pick the crop with highest CLIP similarity to its label, and caption it with Qwen2-VL-7B (Qwen2.5-VL-3B quantized on robot) using a color/material/shape template.
Relevant-object filtering: two Mistral Large 2 queries, first extracting object nouns/modifiers from the utterance, then selecting matching instance IDs from the scene list.

Spatial reasoning toolbox: heuristic functions (find_near/between/above/below/left/right, order_bottom_to_top, order_smallest_to_largest, order_left_to_right, find_objects_near_room_corner). The LLM sees {id,name,caption,cx,cy,cz,size}, and the functions access full boxes; left/right uses signed angle from nearest free-space point.
LLM sequential reasoning: chain-of-thought with a single in-context example produces a series of tool calls and picks the final object ID (GPT-4o or Mistral Large 2).
Action parsing: for deployment the LLM emits go_near/go_between calls that become waypoints for an obstacle-avoiding planner.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o or Mistral Large 2 (frozen) for filtering/reasoning; Qwen2-VL-7B (frozen) for captions; Grounding DINO + SAM2 for mapping
setting.observation: 3D object boxes and names (GT on ScanNet) plus cropped RGB images; on robots 360 camera + 3D LiDAR
setting.action_space: object ID selection; on robot, waypoints (go_near/go_between) to an obstacle-avoidant planner
setting.simulator: none (ScanNet scenes for benchmarks); real world for navigation
setting.privileged: GT bounding boxes/instance segmentation and GT object labels on ReferIt3D/IRef-VLA benchmarks; none in real world

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 sampled statements matching Easy/Hard/View-Dep/View-Ind distribution of the test set
numbers.extra: GT boxes; mean±std over multiple trials

numbers_note: Metric is grounding accuracy (not SR/SPL). Nr3D/Sr3D/IRef-VLA are not canonical names in the list, so listed as other. Captions ablation (Nr3D, GPT-4o) also gives 54.5 overall without captions vs 60.5 with. Real-world results are qualitative only.
results: SORT3D zero-shot gets 62.0% overall on Nr3D (GPT-4o) and 92.0% on Sr3D, competitive with supervised methods (~64-65% Nr3D) but below Transcrib3D (GPT-4o 65.6 Nr3D, 96.5 Sr3D). It beats Transcrib3D on Sr3D view-dependent (95.5 vs 88.9) and IRef-VLA Hard (75.0 vs 57.5). It runs in real time on two robots for object-goal navigation in three unseen environments.
limitations: Depends on online LLM APIs (GPT-4o/Mistral Large 2), so needs internet access
Small evaluation (200 samples per subset), LLM run-to-run variance up to 6%, and few benchmarks for online grounding; real-world tests are qualitative
Fails on pragmatics and compound logic (e.g. choosing a pillow not on the bed), and overall accuracy trails Transcrib3D
